compliance.emc: FCC 47 CFR Part 15 Class A, EN 55022 Class A, ICES-003 Class A, VCCI Class A, AS/NZS CISPR 22 Class A, CISPR 22 Class A, EN 55024, EN 300386, CE
compliance.nebs: GR-1089-CORE EMC and electrical safety for network telecommunications equipment (listed by the datasheet; no level stated)

environmental.acoustic-noise: 39 dBA with a 350 W AC AFO supply; 41.2 dBA with a 550 W DC AFO supply (datasheet Table 3, ISO 7779 at 23 C)
environmental.altitude: up to 3049 m operating (10,000 ft); 4877 m non-operating
environmental.humidity: 10 to 85 percent noncondensing operating; 0 to 95 percent non-operating
environmental.operating-temp: 0 to 45 C (32 to 113 F) for AFO models; 0 to 35 C for AFI models

features.macsec: IEEE 802.1AE on all Gigabit Ethernet and 10 Gigabit Ethernet ports
features.optics-qsfp: 40GbE QSFP+ SR4 (multimode) and DAC direct-attach copper (datasheet, Supported Optics)
features.optics-sfp: LC SFP SX (multimode) and LX (single-mode), and 100BASE-FX and 1000BASE-T copper SFPs on the fixed 100/1000BASE-X ports (datasheet, Supported Optics and Ordering Information)
features.optics-sfp-plus: LC SFP+ SR, USR, LRM (multimode), LR, ER (single-mode) and DAC direct-attach copper (datasheet, Supported Optics)
features.poe: none - the 32-port switches have no Power over Ethernet
features.uplink-module: one slot; 2-port 40-Gigabit EX-UM-2QSFP or 8-port 1/10-Gigabit SFP+ EX-UM-8X8SFP (neither is part of the shipping configuration)
features.virtual-chassis: up to 10 members; the two rear QSFP+ ports are Virtual Chassis ports by default, and the four built-in SFP+ ports cannot be Virtual Chassis ports

management.console: mini-USB on the front, RJ-45 console on the rear
management.lcd: 2 lines of 16 characters with Menu and Enter buttons
management.oob: MGMT RJ-45 with link activity and status lamps (rear)
management.usb: one USB port on the rear

performance.airflow-cfm: fan 22 CFM, each power supply 7.5 CFM; 59 CFM total with two supplies (datasheet)

physical.depth-no-psu: 454.0 mm (17.87 in, 45.4 cm) with no power supply or uplink module (Table 10)
physical.depth-with-uplink: 490.7 mm (19.31 in, 49.07 cm) with a power supply and an uplink module (Table 10)
physical.uplink-module-weight: 0.61 lb (0.28 kg) for the 2-port EX-UM-2QSFP; 0.74 lb (0.34 kg) for the 8-port EX-UM-8X8SFP
physical.weight: 13 lb (5.9 kg) with no power supply and no fan module (guide Table 10, stated for every model but the 48MP); 16.1 lb (7.3 kg) with one power supply and two fan modules (datasheet)

power.psu-redundancy: N+0 or N+N; up to two supplies, one is enough for the chassis

configs.description: EX4300-32F as shipped - one 350 W AC power supply (AIR OUT) in slot 0 with a cover panel over slot 1, two EX4300-FAN (AIR OUT) fan modules, and the uplink slot covered. Front-to-back airflow. EX4300-32F-TAA is the same hardware as a Trade Agreement Act SKU.
configs.name: ac

configs.description: EX4300-32F-DC - one 550 W DC power supply (AIR OUT) in slot 0 with a cover panel over slot 1, two EX4300-FAN (AIR OUT) fan modules, and the uplink slot covered. Front-to-back airflow. EX4300-32F-DC-TAA is the same hardware as a Trade Agreement Act SKU.
configs.name: dc

configs.description: EX4300-32F-S - the spare chassis, shipped with no power supply and no fan module; either AC or DC supplies and AIR OUT or AIR IN fans are ordered separately, and the datasheet's spare-chassis matrix says which combinations are supported. The supply and fan bays are shown open.
configs.name: s

gaps.wanted: Where the two-hole protective earthing terminal sits on the rear panel and its hole pitch. The guide's Table 69 puts it on the rear panel with a two-hole lug and 10-32 screws, and Figure 14 carries no callout for it. A rear photograph or a dimensioned drawing settles it.

A straight-on studio photograph of the front and of the rear. The maker's image library holds none for this model, so the front and rear are read off 1.3 px per mm callout figures and the lamp block follows the 24-port photographs.
Whether the two QSFP+ ports are numbered on the metal. Figure 14 is too coarse to show printing under them; the 24-port model prints 0 to 3 under its four. A rear photograph settles it.
The bracket positions of the front-mounting brackets: no figure in the guide measures them for this model, so no ear position or kit is listed.
A library component for an LCD display; the LCD panel is a decor rectangle until one exists.
The EX-UM-2QSFP and EX-UM-8X8SFP uplink modules and their ports, left for the later uplink-module slice; the bay takes only the cover panel here.

Which supplies the 32-port switch takes: the guide's Table 40 says only the 350 W AC AFO supply, the datasheet's spare-chassis matrix also marks the 1100 W AC AFO and both AFI supplies as supported combinations. The bays follow the guide for the 1100 W supply and the datasheet for the AFI ones; see psu-seating.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 5 bays (front 1, rear 4); `physical-context` on port group sfp - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

airflow.note: Guide Tables 7, 27, 28 and 31: AIR OUT (AFO) is front-to-back and AIR IN (AFI) is back-to-front; this model ships AFO fan modules and an AFO supply (Table 28). The guide's model tables list no AFI SKU of the 32-port switch, so no back-to-front configuration is orderable; the -S chassis accepts AFI parts and a viewer can seat them.

chassis.note: Guide Table 10 and the datasheet: height 1.72 in (4.37 cm) = 43.7 mm; width 17.36 in (44.1 cm) = 441.0 mm, "the outer edges of the front-mounting brackets extend the width to 19 in", so 441.0 is the body between the bracket flanges. Depth for the EX4300-32F, which has its own line in Table 10: 17.87 in (45.4 cm) with no power supply or uplink module, 19 in (48.28 cm) with a power supply installed and 19.31 in (49.07 cm) with a power supply and an uplink module. The datasheet prints 49.1 cm for the last; the guide's 49.07 is carried. The modelled depth is 482.8 mm, the figure with the power supply fitted, as shipped; the other two are in attrs. 1RU.

colour.note: The face is #898d94, the median of bare plate in the 24-port studio photograph, used for the family because no photograph of this model exists. The supply and fan faces carry their own tones (see the components).

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's inventory (Table 68) ships two mounting brackets and mounting screws and says the switch mounts in a two-post or four-post rack; the datasheet lists the kits EX-4PST-RMK (adjustable four-post), EX-RMK (rack-mount) and EX-WMK (wall-mount) as separate items. No figure measures the bracket position for this model, so no ear position is written and no rail kit is listed in chassis.kits. The kit part numbers are recorded here for the later dedupe.

fan-legends.note: Figure 14 callout 8, "Fan module slot numbers and LEDs": a fan legend and a status LED sit beside each fan module, to the left of fan 0 (x 283.5) and to the right of fan 1 (x 395). Their text is two or three glyphs in a 1.3 px per mm raster; a slot number is printed, the symbol is not resolved. The status lamp is Table 29's: green when the module works, unlit when absent, failed or of the other airflow.

front-ports.note: 32 SFP cages in four gangs of four columns by two rows, read off Figure 10 at 1.288 px per mm. The gang outlines start at 103.5, 167.7, 231.9 and 296.1 mm and are 59.2 mm wide, so the column pitch is 14.8 mm (the dividers between columns are 19.06 px apart) and the gutter is 5.0 mm; the last gang ends at 354.8 mm, which 16 columns at 14.8 plus three gutters of 5.0 reproduces (251.8 mm). The registry's sfp-ganged pitch is 14.25, a cage width, not a spacing the figure confirms, so the figure's pitch is used and the cage cutouts stand 0.55 mm apart. The two rows span 9.7 to 35.1 mm down, which is the registry's 15.0 mm row pitch plus one 10.4 mm cage. The stacked pair follows the library's rule: the upper cage upright and the lower turned 180 (decided by the rule, not observed; see mx204's stack-orientation note).

front-right.note: The LCD block follows the 24-port and 48-port EX4300 devices, whose positions were read off Juniper's photographs at 3.29 px per mm: LCD window 377.2 to 412.8 x 6.8 to 16.4 mm; the EX4300 legend above it; Menu and Enter buttons at x 422.2; three chassis status lamps at x 428.9; a face screw each side at (367.4, 12.8) and (436.0, 13.1). Figure 10 agrees with them within 1.9 mm (LCD 375.3 to 413.3, buttons 420.6, lamps 427.8, screws 367.2 and 436.3), which is two of its pixels. The four SFP+ cages read 359.5 to 419.3 x 24.8 to 34.9 mm (four at the same 14.8 pitch), and the mini-USB console jack reads at (431.3, 32.4) with CON1 printed below it, both off Figure 10. The 32-port front prints the model as EX4300-32F in the figure; the 24-port photographs print EX4300.

fru-bays.note: Two power supply bays (PSU 0, PSU 1) and two fan bays (0, 1), each seating the guide's FRU parts. No supply or fan is built into the chassis: all are FRUs. Mixing AFO and AFI parts, or AC and DC, is forbidden by the guide and is left to the configuration: a bay lists every part it can take and a configuration seats a matching set. The cover panel the guide ships for an empty supply slot is seated in slot 1 as shipped. Guide Power Supplies: the EX4300-32F does not support DC power, while the EX4300-32F-S and EX4300-32F-DC do, so DC supplies are seated in the -DC configuration only.

gate-1-front.note: THE FRONT FIGURE PASSES, AT LOW RESOLUTION. Guide Figure 10 (g022130) is a flat front elevation, a 609 x 158 px raster: the chassis outline is 568 px across (x 2 to 570) and 56 px down (51.3 to 107.3), aspect 10.1 against the stated 441.0 / 43.7 = 10.09, so it is orthographic and carries geometry, at 1.288 px per mm. One pixel is 0.78 mm, so every front position is good to about one millimetre and is estimated. The isometric Figure 3 gives counts only.

gate-1-rear.note: THE REAR FIGURE PASSES, AT LOW RESOLUTION. Guide Figure 14 (g022131) is a flat rear elevation, 586 x 165 px: the chassis outline is 566 px across (x 5 to 571) for 441.0 mm, 1.285 px per mm, and the top edge sits at row 56.5, so a face 43.7 mm tall would end at row 112.7 where the figure's bottom outline is drawn. Positions are good to about one millimetre and are estimated.

interface-names.note: Not printed and not modelled. The guide's factory-default configuration names the network ports ge-0/0/0 to ge-0/0/31 and the uplink module ports ge-0/2/n and xe-0/2/n; no table gives the SFP+ or QSFP+ ports' names.

lamp-legends.note: drawing-vs-photo for the sibling, and no photograph of this model: the guide says the three chassis lamps are labeled ALM, SYS and MST, but Juniper's photographs of the 24-port and 48-port models show three bare lamps with no legend. Figure 10's lamp block is the same as those models', so no legend is drawn. The order top to bottom is the guide's order of naming (ALM, SYS, MST); no document states it, so it is estimated.

lcd.note: The LCD panel shows two lines of 16 characters (guide, LCD Panel in EX4300 Switches). It is drawn as the dark green window the sibling photographs show; no library component exists for a display and none is added, so it is a decor rectangle and not a part.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life notice on 2026-10-23. Third-party trackers disagree and none reaches Juniper's own bulletin: one gives announcement and last order together on 2026-03-31 (TSB105633), another gives an announcement of 2022-06-24 with last order 2024-03-31. Both end support on 2029-03-31, which is the only date carried; the sale date is left out because the two disagree. Recorded as announced, estimated.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat: the guide's front and rear figures show them in perspective with a logo on the lid and mounting holes in the sides. Each carries an `empty` sentence.

port-lamps.note: Guide Network Port, Built-In QSFP+ Port, Uplink Port, and Uplink Module Port LEDs, Figure 31 and Tables 21 and 22: each SFP network port has two lamps, a Link activity lamp (green, blinking with activity, steady when linked) and a Status lamp whose meaning is chosen with the LCD Enter button (ADM, DPX or SPD; the 32-port switches have no PoE). Figure 31 draws four small arrows between the upper and lower cage of a column, the Link/Activity and Status arrows of the lower port and of the upper port. They are placed there, in the library's arrow lamps, with the pairing of arrows to windows read from the EX4100 devices, which draw the same four arrows; which arrow is which within a column is not stated by any document held. Each SFP+ uplink port has two square lamps (Figure 33, Table 23), one either side of its number; the left one is taken as Link activity and the right as Status, which no document states.

port-numbering.note: Figure 10 prints the numbers in pairs under each column, 0 and 1 under the first column, 2 and 3 under the second, up to 30 and 31, with the even number set higher and the odd lower beside it. The even number belongs to the upper cage and the odd to the lower, so numbering runs down each column and then across, as on the 24-port and 48-port models. The four SFP+ ports are numbered 0 to 3 between their lamps. The numeral offsets are read at 1.288 px per mm and are estimated. The guide's CLI interface names (ge-0/0/0 to ge-0/0/31, and ge-0/2/n and xe-0/2/n on the uplink module) are not printed on the metal and are not modelled; no table gives the SFP+ ports' names.

power.note: Guide Table 33 and the datasheet. The base power the system needs is 164 W; one 350 W AC supply gives 350 W usable and two give 665 W (Table 33). The 32-port switches have no PoE (guide, Table 2 and Table 33 note). The 550 W DC supply's rating gives its own table (Table 49), and the DC supply does not support PoE. No typical or maximum draw of the switch itself is stated by either document.

psu-seating.note: SOURCES DISAGREE on what the 32-port switch takes. Guide Table 40 says "the 32-port EX4300 switches support only 350 W AC power supplies with front-to-back airflow direction", Table 2 says the switches "support power supply and fan module with front-to-back airflow direction" and ships the -DC with a 550 W AIR OUT supply, while Table 2's -S row says to order fans labelled "either AIR OUT (AFO) or AIR IN (AFI)", and the datasheet's spare-chassis matrix marks the EX4300-32F-S as taking the 1100 W AC AFO supply, both 350 W and 550 W AFI supplies and the 550 W DC AFO supply, and not the 715 W or 1400 W ones. The bays take the supplies both documents allow (350 W AC AFO and 550 W DC AFO), the AFI variants of those two (datasheet Y, and the guide's own AFI fan statement), the cover panel, and not the 1100 W, 715 W or 1400 W supplies; the 1100 W supply rests on the datasheet alone and the newer guide denies it. The fan bays take both airflows.

rear.note: Guide Figure 14, 1.285 px per mm, rear seen from behind with x = 0 at the left of the drawing: power supply slot 0 from 9.9 mm and slot 1 from 101.7 mm, each 84.0 mm wide (their module edges read 9.9 to 93.4 and 101.8 to 185.3), a vent field from 188.5 to 280.0, the serial number label (callout 10) at 189.2 to 212.6 x 20.3 to 25.1, two QSFP+ ports from 217.5 on the registry's 19.0 mm pitch with four small lamps below (centres 223.8, 230.9, 242.9 and 249.9 at y 38.4), fan module 0 from 288.5 and fan module 1 from 340.2 (each about 49 to 51 mm across, the 48.6 mm face used), the ESD point at (409.5, 5.0), the vertical USB port at (406.1, 28.7), and the management and console jacks from 416.5 to 433.5. The management and console jacks are drawn at the 24-port model's 15.8 x 13.2 mm and 14.2 mm spacing, because Figure 14's jacks (16.4 and 10.9 mm tall) are too coarse to size them. Small circles at the left edge of slot 0, beside slot 1 and beside the vent field that no callout names are not modelled.

rear-ground.note: The guide says the protective earthing terminal of the EX4300 is on the rear panel (Table 69: two-hole terminal, two 10-32 screws, Panduit LCD10-10A-L lug) but no figure for this model identifies it or gives its pitch. It is not modelled; see gaps.

rear-qsfp-lamps.note: Guide Figure 14 callout 9 and Figure 32: each QSFP+ port has two lamps below it, a Link activity lamp and a Status lamp (Table 24: steady green when the 40-Gigabit port is up). Four small rectangles below the pair, 7.1 mm apart about each port's centre. The lamps' roles within a pair are not stated. Figure 14 is too coarse to show whether the two ports carry a printed number, so none is drawn (see gaps).

slot-legends.note: Figure 14 callout 11, "Power supply slot numbers": one legend at the left of slot 0 (x 5.7) and one between the two supplies (x 97.3). Slot 0 is taken as the left one, as the guide lists "AC power supplies in slot 0 and slot 1" and slot 0 of the fans is the left; no figure labels a number on the drawing legibly, so which supply is 0 is estimated.

sources.note: EX4300 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, published 2025-08-12 (414 pages; https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex4300/ex4300.pdf): Figures 3 and 4 (isometric panel drawings), Figures 10 and 14 (flat callout figures g022130 and g022131), Table 2 and Table 8 (the 32-port models and what each ships with), Tables 4, 5 and 7 (uplink modules and supply airflow), Table 10 (chassis size and weight), Tables 18 to 29 (LEDs), Tables 27, 28, 30, 31, 40, 47 and 48 (fans and supplies), Table 33 (power budget) and Table 68 (cover panels). EX4300 Line of Ethernet Switches Datasheet (https://www.juniper.net/content/dam/www/assets/datasheets/us/en/switches/ex4300-line-of-ethernet-switches-datasheet.pdf, 17 pages, PDF created 2022-07-25): Table 1 (models), Table 2 (spare-chassis matrix), Table 3 (acoustics), physical and environmental specifications, ordering information. Both documents were fetched from juniper.net on 2026-10-23 and carry the sha256 values below. Juniper's image library holds no photograph of the EX4300-32F: ex4300-32f-front-high.jpg, ex4300-32f-rear-high.jpg and the same under the ex4300 and ex4300-32f folders each returned an HTML 404 page, tried once. The held intake folders for Juniper (exqfx, mx/visio) are not present on this host, so no held photograph, stencil or model was used. The NetBox device-type library was not consulted. Terms of use: the guide and datasheet are Juniper's, published for customers; none of it is copied into the library, only transcribed facts and new drawings.

uplink-slot.note: The 32-port switches carry the uplink slot as the large opening at the left end of the front, 86.8 x 40.7 mm by Figure 10 (callout 1, "Cover panel for uplink module slot"), against the small slot under the LCD of the 24 and 48-port models. The guide supports two modules in it, the 2-port 40-Gigabit EX-UM-2QSFP (Table 5) and the 8-port 1/10-Gigabit EX-UM-8X8SFP, neither of which is in the library; the bay takes only the cover panel here and both are left for a later slice. Uplink modules are not part of the shipping configuration and the guide's inventory (Table 68) says a cover panel is provided.

variants.note: The guide's 32-port models are EX4300-32F, EX4300-32F-DC and EX4300-32F-S (Tables 2 and 8). All three share this front panel, so each is a configuration of this device: ac, dc and s. The datasheet also lists the Trade Agreement Act SKUs EX4300-32F-TAA and EX4300-32F-DC-TAA, the same hardware ordered under another number; they are carried as extra part numbers of the ac and dc configurations. The guide's other models (EX4300-24T, -24P, -48T, -48P and their -S, -AFI and -DC variants) are separate devices on main; the EX4300-48MP is the second device of this slice.
